answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a deposit in a public ledger before bidding. After verified delivery, the buyer pays and the agent can reclaim its stake; proven fraud burns part of it. A sybil attacker must therefore fund each fake identity separately and keep that capital unavailable, while risking losses for each dishonest bid. The copper stake creates a visible ledge to cross, and adding identities makes the required capital ripple upward.
